summary: Adds three GET endpoints to the directory API: a user search backed by SQL, an in-memory per-key request counter, and an upstream status probe. main.go wires them onto the mux.

findings.title: SQL query built from the name query parameter
findings.problem: Search interpolates the name query parameter directly into the SQL text with Sprintf. Nothing escapes or validates the value before QueryContext runs it.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can inject SQL and read or alter every table in the database.
findings.fix: Pass the name as a bound parameter to QueryContext instead of formatting it into the string.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex stays locked on the missing-key return
findings.problem: Count locks h.mu on line 60 and then returns on line 63 without unlocking when key is empty. The only Unlock sits on line 67, after that return.
findings.consequence: One request to GET /count without a key leaves the mutex held forever. Every later Count request blocks on Lock and the endpoint hangs.
findings.fix: Validate key before taking the lock, or use defer h.mu.Unlock() right after Lock.

findings.title: Body closed before the error check in fetchStatus
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close() on line 83 before checking err on line 84. When http.Get fails, resp is nil and the deferred call dereferences a nil pointer.
findings.consequence: Any upstream failure panics the handler goroutine, so GET /upstream drops the connection instead of returning 502. The error branch in Upstream never runs.
findings.fix: Check err first and only defer the Close after the error check.

findings.title: Row iteration error ignored in Search
findings.problem: Search never calls rows.Err() after the rows.Next() loop ends. A connection or driver error during iteration ends the loop silently.
findings.consequence: Clients receive a 200 response with a truncated user list when the database fails mid-query.
findings.fix: Check rows.Err() after the loop and answer with a 500 when it is set.

findings.title: Upstream request has no timeout
findings.problem: fetchStatus uses http.Get, which runs on the default client with no timeout. The handler also ignores the request context.
findings.consequence: A slow or hanging upstream holds every GET /upstream goroutine open indefinitely and can exhaust the server.
findings.fix: Build the request with the handler's context and send it through a client with a Timeout set.

findings.title: New endpoints have no covering tests
findings.problem: The change adds Search, Count, Upstream and fetchStatus with several error branches. The repository contains no test files, so none of this behaviour is exercised.
findings.consequence: The locking, error and parsing bugs in these handlers would have surfaced in a basic httptest run.
findings.fix: Add httptest handler tests for the success path and each error branch. Cover the empty key and failed upstream cases.

dropped.reason: This reports the same SQL string on the same line already raised under c1, and one finding per problem applies.
